title: Words That Reveal Stance
text:
Many readers assume that a strong opinion must be expressed with dramatic words. In fact, skilled writers often reveal their stance through subtle choices, such as hedging phrases like 'it seems' or 'arguably'. These words signal that the writer is confident enough to admit uncertainty. Consequently, careful language can be more persuasive than loud claims.

However, not every hedge is a sign of weakness. Some critics argue that excessive qualification makes a text vague and difficult to trust. Readers, therefore, must judge whether a writer's caution is honest or merely evasive. In the end, the way an author frames an argument often tells us more than the argument itself.

questions.text: According to the passage, what can skilled writers reveal through subtle choices?

What does the writer imply about hedging phrases such as 'it seems' or 'arguably'?
options: They show the writer is uncertain about everything

questions.text: Why must readers judge a writer's caution carefully?
options: Because caution can be honest or merely evasive

paragraph_translations: Muchos lectores suponen que una opinión firme debe expresarse con palabras dramáticas. De hecho, los escritores hábiles a menudo revelan su postura mediante elecciones sutiles, como frases de cautela del tipo 'parece que' o 'podría argumentarse'. Estas palabras indican que el autor tiene la confianza suficiente para admitir la incertidumbre. Por consiguiente, un lenguaje cuidadoso puede resultar más persuasivo que las afirmaciones rotundas.

Sin embargo, no toda cautela es señal de debilidad. Algunos críticos sostienen que una calificación excesiva vuelve el texto vago y difícil de creer. Por ello, los lectores deben juzgar si la prudencia del autor es honesta o simplemente evasiva. Al final, la forma en que un autor plantea un argumento suele decirnos más que el propio argumento.
